key_insight: An agent-guided multi-fidelity learning workflow can detect and correct numerical instabilities in GW-Bethe-Salpeter calculations, yielding more reliable quasiparticle gaps and exciton binding energies for strained MoS2-WS2 bilayers.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to faster, more trustworthy excited-state property prediction for optoelectronic materials screening and design, especially where high-fidelity calculations are too expensive for exhaustive use.
method: A structural agent flags fragile or inconsistent calculations and assigns confidence weights to select reference points.
Machine learning transfers information across related stacking, strain, and k-point sampling conditions.
Gaussian process correction restores smoother excited-state trends while preserving physical strain dependence and calibrated uncertainty.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved agreement with higher-fidelity references than a no-agent baseline across stacking registries, strain branches, and reciprocal-space samplings, while catching spike-like artifacts and near-zero-gap collapses.
watch_item: Performance depends on the agent correctly identifying numerical failures, so the approach may be less reliable if the instability patterns are not represented in the training/reference set.
paper_title: Agentic multi-fidelity learning of quasiparticle and excitonic properties
